policy-based coordination can provide a foundation for the coordination of joint human-agent activity, and that this foundation can be implemented within the context of a services framework.
policy-based coordination in human-agent joint activity is a promising approach that is grounded in theory and has been demonstrated to support a range of joint activities.

1) the coordination of human-agent activity requires a policy-based approach; 2) policies must be expressed in a language that is both human and machine interpretable; 3) policies must be able to represent the dynamic and contingent nature of joint activity; 4) policy execution must be able to handle the inherent uncertainty of joint activity; and 5) policy-based coordination must be able to adapt to changes in the joint activity.
